content.comment_body: Hello, I am working on retrofitting an oven for monitoring that currently uses a K39 controller ([url]). I'm looking for advice on integrating Modbus RTU oven controllers via a gateway. My search through the forum hasn't resolved my problem yet. I'm open to using either [company_name] PLCs or [product_name] PLCs for this purpose. Any suggestions are welcome and I'm not expecting a full solution. Kind regards, [user_name]

Depending on how the K39 controller is being used, it might be worth considering a [product_name] PLC instead of the K39 controller. It's important to know the current function of the K39 controller—is it simply switching the oven on and off based on temperature? A [product_name] PLC with a temperature sensor could handle this. If you prefer to use the K39 controller, please provide more details, such as the full Modbus table and your monitoring goals with the [product_name] PLC. You'll need at least a [product_name] with [version_no] to utilize Modbus TCP and a gateway from Modbus RTU to Modbus TCP. Do you already have a gateway or a link to a gateway you plan to use? Regards, [user_name]
There are TCP/Modbus server devices that can serve as a bridge between MODBUS TCP and MODBUS RTU. Consider researching King Pigeon hardware as an option, for example: [url]
The total cost of using the controller plus a Modbus server box may be higher than simply using a [product_name] and an analog module.
Alternatively, you can use a Linux computer equipped with RS485 ports to run a gateway between Modbus TCP and Modbus RTU. For instance: [url]

The discussion revolves around the trade-offs of using a protocol gateway versus replacing the controller with a [product_name] PLC or expansion module, with cost, complexity, and integration effort being considered.

They seek advice on suitable hardware or gateway options that will work with [company_name] PLCs.
